en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Eighteenth Chapter
Is it not the case that there is no compassion in the Buddha, the Blessed One?
Yes, it is.
Is it not the case that there is no loving-kindness in the Buddha, the Blessed One?
One should not say so...
Is it not the case that there is no compassion in the Buddha, the Blessed One? One should not say so.
“Yes.
“Does the Buddha, the Blessed One, lack sympathetic joy … [and] equanimity?”
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is there loving-kindness (mettā) in the Buddha, the Blessed One? Yes.
“Does the Buddha, the Blessed One, possess compassion?
“One should not say so.
…pe… “Does the Buddha, the Blessed One, possess sympathetic joy? …pe…
Is it equanimity?
Yes. Does the Buddha, the Blessed One, possess compassion? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is it not the case that there is no compassion in the Buddha, the Blessed One?
Yes, it is.
“Is the Blessed One lacking in compassion?
“One should not say so.
…pe… “Is it not true that the Blessed One is compassionate, a benefactor of the world, one who feels sympathy for the world, and one who acts for the welfare of the world?”
“Yes.

“If it is true that the Blessed One is compassionate, a benefactor of the world, one who feels sympathy for the world, and one who acts for the welfare of the world, then surely, sir, you should not say:
‘The Buddha, the Blessed One, has no compassion’ … [and so on] …”
Is it not the case that there is no compassion in the Buddha, the Blessed One?
Yes, it is.
But did the Blessed One not indeed enter the meditative attainment of great compassion?
“Yes.
If the Blessed One entered the attainment of great compassion, then indeed it should not be said:
“There is no compassion in the Buddha, the Blessed One.”
Is there compassion in the Buddha, the Blessed One?
Yes. Is the Blessed One possessed of lust? No.
If you do not say so,
then it follows that there is no compassion in the Buddha, the Blessed One.
The Discussion on Compassion is finished.
